summary: Browser upload preflight storm (parallel OPTIONS) causing tenant-wide 429s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightMap reports persistent 429 throttles for a small cohort of users while performing file uploads from a browser uploader widget. The pattern looks like tenant-wide token exhaustion that correlates with large numbers of parallel CORS preflight (OPTIONS) requests from the browser clients.

Impact:
- Intermittent but repeated 429s for upload API (multipart start/complete) for ~50 users during peak import windows.
- Client retries amplify the problem and cause other routes for the tenant to hit soft throttles.
- Affects scheduled ingest and interactive uploads; revenue-impacting for BrightMap (dedicated contract).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (tenant-dedicated) in us-west-2
- Browser-based uploader using signed ephemeral URLs with 5m TTL generated by BrightMap backend
- Traffic originates from multiple client subnets behind CDN and some mid-tier proxies

Observed behaviour:
- Spike of OPTIONS requests (CORS preflight) immediately before POSTs for multipart uploads.
- Rate limiter counts appear to include OPTIONS preflights and treat them as token-consuming requests against the tenant quota.
- 429 responses include X-RateLimit headers showing token window exhausted; console shows many concurrent OPTIONS in flight.

Expected behaviour:
- Preflight (OPTIONS) should not consume the same quota as POSTs for token accounting, or there should be guidance on isolating preflight traffic into a low-weight path.

Logs / samples attached in comments below and in linked GH issue for edge-proxy gating changes.

Key timestamps:
- First report: 2026-03-01 09:12 PDT
- Reproduced by support: 2026-03-01 10:05 PDT
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure browser uploader to perform parallel file chunk uploads (N=8) with signed ephemeral URL per chunk.
2) Start upload from Chrome/Safari behind a CDN so each chunk triggers CORS preflight (OPTIONS) before POST.
3) Observe server-side ingress (edge-proxy) and rate-limiter metrics for tenant token consumption.
4) Repeat at scale (20 concurrent browser clients) to trigger tenant token exhaustion and 429s.
5) Optionally enable client retries to see amplification pattern.
comments: 2026-03-01 10:20 - Ethan Cole: I can reproduce in staging with a small harness that fires OPTIONS + POST pairs. Looks like the edge increments the tenant token counter on OPTIONS. Created GH PR to instrument counting: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/412

2026-03-01 12:05 - Support (Ana Gomez): Shared quick mitigation to customer: reduce parallelism to 2-3 per client and increase ephemeral URL TTL to 15m to reduce preflight frequency. Customer acknowledged and applied immediately; reported partial relief.
2026-03-02 09:40 - SRE (Leo Huang): Deployed temporary rate-smoothing rule for tenant to give 30% burst headroom for upload endpoints while we analyze proper counting semantics.

2026-03-03 14:10 - Customer (BrightMap - Ryan L): Asking for configuration options in Dedicated console to treat OPTIONS requests as 'non-billed' for quota or to route preflight to a separate, low-weight ingress.
investigation_notes: Edge-proxy currently increments rate-limiter token for all HTTP methods by default; no method-based exemption configured.
OPTIONS requests typically do not have payload and are safe to classify as low-cost; counting them against the same token pool causes small requests to consume quota quickly when parallelized.
We measured a 4x increase in perceived token consumption during a 5-minute upload window where clients used 8 parallel chunk uploads.
Related config: dedicated pool rate-limiter has single tenant token bucket applied across all routes; no per-route isolation for upload-preflight vs upload-data.
Edge-proxy PR 412 adds instrumentation and switch to exclude OPTIONS from token accounting behind a feature flag for testing.
resolution: Short-term mitigation (applied 2026-03-02): enabled tenant-level rate-smoothing to provide extra burst capacity for upload routes and advised customer to lower client parallelism and lengthen URL TTL.

Medium-term plan: ship edge-proxy feature flag to ignore OPTIONS for quota accounting in Dedicated (PR 412). After internal testing, flip flag for affected dedicated tenants and monitor for regressions.

Long-term: expose console toggle in Dedicated to set method-based quota exemptions and add per-route lightweight quota pools (upload-preflight pool vs upload-data pool). Add docs describing best practices for browser upload flows (recommended parallelism, TTLs, and client backoff).
Follow-ups: create INT task to add automated test to e2e suite validating CORS preflight does not consume standard token quota for dedicated tenants with exemption enabled (INT-2209).
